title: Treasure in Jars of Clay
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: God chose frail people to carry the light of his glory, so that the surpassing power would be seen as his and not ours.
exhortation: If you think about it, it's a strange thing that God chose humans to display the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. It seems to me there were better options. God didn't choose angels or seraphim or the heavenly creatures Scripture speaks of to display the light of the knowledge of his glory. He didn't even choose Solomon's magnificent temple as the permanent home for his glory. He chose humans.

Left to ourselves, I think we'd all be very aware that we are pretty poor vessels. Here we're described as jars of clay: temporary, easily broken, not particularly beautiful. On the surface it doesn't seem to make sense. We are far more frail than angels, not half so strong and glorious as Solomon's temple. So why?
Paul answers the question: to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us. Our frailty magnifies God's glory, and that is by design. It's built into what God is doing.

So this morning, if you are very aware of your weakness and frailty, I hope this is a comfort and an encouragement to you. God designed it this way, so that in your frailty, your weakness and your inability, his Holy Spirit would empower you and work through you for his glory. Hear the words the Lord spoke to Paul: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." And add your voice to Paul's when he says, "Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me." What an encouragement.
prayer: Lord, may you be our all in all. I pray that we wouldn't try to run this race, walk this path, defeat this sin or change this person, whatever it is, in our own power. Let us look to you and your power, and find your power in our weakness. You oppose the proud and lift up the humble. Help us humble ourselves under your mighty hand as we go through our day.

Remind us of our weakness, Lord, but don't leave us there. Fill us with your power and remind us that we are strong in you, not in ourselves. I pray that this would give us joy and faith as we look ahead to the day, so that whatever seems daunting ahead of us, we will see your power first. In Jesus' name, amen.
